fields.description:
## Context

A 200 from `/health` does not establish that the container can serve an MCP request, yet it is the
only thing the blue-green cutover waits for. `/health` is a FastMCP `custom_route` registered
deliberately OUTSIDE the auth middleware and the DNS-rebinding guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, `register_health_route`), and
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` polls `GET http://127.0.0.1:<newport>/health` until 200 and flips
the nginx upstream — the deploy path never issues one `/mcp` request. Measured on the box 2026-08-28: `/health` 200 at 20:21:29.87,
cutover 20:21:30, first `/mcp` request 20:22:24 — promoted 54 s before it served one. A
container whose `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not admit the hostname real traffic carries
answers `/health` 200 while 421-ing every real request, and the deploy promotes it. Same class as
`mobile-groovy-badger` (a storeless container passing this gate), which established that `/health`
must carry enough signal for the gate to mean something.

## Approach

Drive one real `initialize` through this server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` inside the
ASGI lifespan — after the session manager is running, before Starlette answers
`lifespan.startup.complete` — and publish the outcome as a `handshake` object on `/health` beside
`in_flight` and `store`. Uvicorn accepts no connection until lifespan startup completes (Starlette's `Router.lifespan`
sends `lifespan.startup.complete` only after entering the lifespan context), so a later `/health`
200 proves by construction that this container has already served an MCP handshake. Only that ordering
buys the implication, so the probe is no background task or lazy `/health` field.

**Conclusive.** The probe calls `mcp.session_manager.handle_request(scope, receive, send)` — the
same entry point the `/mcp` route serves through (`StreamableHTTPASGIApp(self._session_manager)`,
`mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:970`). A 200 cannot be produced unless the transport-security guard
admitted the Host, `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` parsed the body, the session manager's task
group started a server task, and `Server.run` answered the `initialize` JSON-RPC request. A throwaway in-process
probe against a `FastMCP` built as `build_server` builds it returned 200 in 3.0 ms with an
admitting allowlist and 421 "Invalid Host header" in 2.1 ms with a non-admitting one. Boundary:
the drive does not traverse `RequireAuthMiddleware`/`ProxyAuthMiddleware` — the server holds no
credential to present to itself, so an auth-enabled boot would always report failure; the
handshake proves the transport + protocol path, not auth config.

**Bounded.** The drive runs under `anyio.fail_after(budget)` with module constant
`DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10`, wrapped so a `TimeoutError`, any `Exception`, or a
non-200 status becomes a reported failure record rather than a raise; boot then continues. The
timeout scope and clock are injected parameters (`fail_after=anyio.fail_after`,
`monotonic=time.monotonic`) — the seam `drain_then_exit(..., sleep=, monotonic=)` already uses
here — so the bound is provable with a fake clock instead of by sleeping.

**Probe Host** (`select_probe_host`) is a total function of the server's own
`TransportSecuritySettings` and bind: (1) the first `allowed_hosts` entry that is a literal host
(no `*`) — on the box `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:359`),
what real traffic carries; (2) else the first `host:*` entry materialized as `host:<bind port>`,
the form `_validate_host` matches (`mcp/server/transport_security.py`); (3) else the bind address,
`0.0.0.0`/`::` normalized to `127.0.0.1`. An allowlist admitting nothing usable — empty, or only unsupported wildcard forms such as
`*.example.com`, which `_validate_host` can never match — falls to (3) and is refused 421 by its
own guard: the AC-2 case. Sourcing the Host from the allowlist rather than the bind is deliberate:
the box binds `0.0.0.0:8091` (`docker-compose.yml:337`) and allows only the public hostname, so a
bind-addressed probe would report a correct production container as failed.

The deploy gate closes as the store gate did (`autodeploy.sh` step 5b): after `/health` 200,
refuse the upstream flip when `handshake.ok` is present and false; an absent field promotes
(mixed-version safety, as the `store` gate already treats an older container).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — `select_probe_host`, the ASGI `initialize` drive, the bounded
  never-raising `run_startup_handshake`, `install_startup_handshake` (wraps
  `app.router.lifespan_context`, unwrapping the `ProxyAuthMiddleware` wrapper when present), the
  `handshake` field on `/health`, and its call from `run_http_with_grace`. 372 LOC today; the
  addition stays well under the 800 cap.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` — the new unit tests.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` — pin the new `/health` `handshake` key.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — readiness gate on `handshake.ok`, mirroring 5b.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — deploy-gate tests on the existing `mcp_box`
  harness, which already stubs per-port `/health` bodies.

No new config key: the budget is a module constant, for the reason the module docstring records
for `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` (a key ripples into `MCP_ENV_VARS` / `server.json`).

## Testing

Every assertion is anchored: each test first proves the handshake actually RAN (a recorded drive
count, or the record's presence) and only then asserts its outcome — an assertion that passes when
the handshake never ran is this bug restated. Both directions are covered (an admitting allowlist
passes AND a non-admitting one fails), the bound is proved with an injected clock rather than a
sleep, and each production edit is then reverted individually with the targeted test required to
fail (return code checked, seed confirmed applied). Tests are named per criterion
below, plus one covering `select_probe_host`'s three branches.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A correctly configured server reports a successful startup handshake on `/health`:
      `test_correctly_configured_server_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts the drive counter
      incremented and the record is `{"ok": True, "status": 200}` with numeric `elapsed_ms`.
- [ ] A server whose transport-security host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports the
      handshake as failed with the refusing status instead of reporting ready:
      `test_unadmitted_probe_host_is_reported_as_failed_with_421` asserts `ok is False`,
      `status == 421`.
- [ ] A handshake that exceeds its budget is reported as a failure and boot continues:
      `test_a_hanging_drive_is_bounded_by_the_budget` (injected clock, no sleep) asserts the call
      returns a failure record naming the timeout.
- [ ] A handshake whose drive raises never propagates the exception:
      `test_a_raising_drive_is_reported_not_propagated` asserts the failure record carries the
      message and the lifespan still yields.
- [ ] The handshake completes inside the ASGI lifespan before uvicorn accepts its first
      connection: `test_handshake_is_recorded_before_lifespan_startup_complete` drives the raw
      ASGI lifespan protocol and asserts the record exists before `lifespan.startup.complete`.
- [ ] The blue-green cutover refuses to promote a container reporting a failed handshake:
      `test_failed_handshake_container_is_not_promoted` asserts `mcp-handshake-failed` is logged,
      the upstream include is byte-identical, nginx not reloaded, the container removed.
- [ ] A container whose `/health` predates the field is still promoted (mixed-version safety):
      `test_container_with_no_handshake_field_still_promotes` asserts the upstream flips.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the affected test modules exit 0 in-session, and each
      production edit reverted individually makes its targeted test fail (return code checked).
